intro.TrustedMarkup:
Narrow number formats for storage: Float16, BFloat16, the two FP8 formats, the OCP MX blocks, the NVFP4 block and packed Int4. A program widens a value to Float32, computes, and narrows the result; the narrow types have no arithmetic of their own.

Every conversion is integer code over the Float32 bit view, so every engine gives the same bits. toFloat32 is exact. A narrowing rounds half to even and gives infinity past the largest finite value where the format has one, else NaN; its Sat form gives the largest finite value. A NaN narrows to the format's NaN code with the sign cleared. BFloat16 is Float32 rounded to its upper 16 bits, subnormals kept.

sig.TrustedMarkup: protocol Narrow { fn toFloat32(self) -> Float32 }

prose.TrustedMarkup: A value that widens to Float32 exactly.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type Float16 = { f16: UInt16 }

prose.TrustedMarkup: IEEE-754 binary16: a sign, 5 exponent bits with bias 15 and 10 mantissa bits. Its largest finite value is 65504 and its NaN code 0x7E00.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn toFloat16(x: Float32) -> Float16

prose.TrustedMarkup: The Float16 nearest x: infinity where x rounds past 65504.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn toFloat16Sat(x: Float32) -> Float16

prose.TrustedMarkup: The Float16 nearest x: 65504 where x rounds past it.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type BFloat16 = { bf16: UInt16 }

prose.TrustedMarkup: The upper 16 bits of a Float32: a sign, 8 exponent bits with bias 127 and 7 mantissa bits. Its NaN code is 0x7FC0.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn toBFloat16(x: Float32) -> BFloat16

prose.TrustedMarkup: The BFloat16 nearest x: infinity where x rounds past the largest finite value.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn toBFloat16Sat(x: Float32) -> BFloat16

prose.TrustedMarkup: The BFloat16 nearest x: the largest finite value where x rounds past it.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type Float8E4M3 = { e4m3: UInt8 }

prose.TrustedMarkup: OCP FP8 E4M3: a sign, 4 exponent bits with bias 7 and 3 mantissa bits. It has no infinity; its largest finite value is 448 and its NaN code 0x7F.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn toFloat8E4M3(x: Float32) -> Float8E4M3

prose.TrustedMarkup: The Float8E4M3 nearest x: NaN where x rounds past 448, an infinity included.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn toFloat8E4M3Sat(x: Float32) -> Float8E4M3

prose.TrustedMarkup: The Float8E4M3 nearest x: 448 where x rounds past it.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type Float8E5M2 = { e5m2: UInt8 }

prose.TrustedMarkup: OCP FP8 E5M2: a sign, 5 exponent bits with bias 15 and 2 mantissa bits. Its largest finite value is 57344 and its NaN code 0x7E.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn toFloat8E5M2(x: Float32) -> Float8E5M2

prose.TrustedMarkup: The Float8E5M2 nearest x: infinity where x rounds past 57344.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn toFloat8E5M2Sat(x: Float32) -> Float8E5M2

prose.TrustedMarkup: The Float8E5M2 nearest x: 57344 where x rounds past it.

sig.TrustedMarkup: protocol Block { /// The value of element `i`, or NaN in a block whose scale is NaN. fn valueAt(self, i: Int64) -> Float32 }

prose.TrustedMarkup: A block of elements that share one scale.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type MxFp8E4M3Block = { e8m0: UInt8, e4m3: Array<UInt8, 32> }

prose.TrustedMarkup: MXFP8 with E4M3 elements.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn toMxFp8E4M3(xs: read Array<Float32, 32>) -> MxFp8E4M3Block

prose.TrustedMarkup: The MXFP8 E4M3 block of xs.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type MxFp8E5M2Block = { e8m0: UInt8, e5m2: Array<UInt8, 32> }

prose.TrustedMarkup: MXFP8 with E5M2 elements.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn toMxFp8E5M2(xs: read Array<Float32, 32>) -> MxFp8E5M2Block

prose.TrustedMarkup: The MXFP8 E5M2 block of xs.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type MxFp6E2M3Block = { e8m0: UInt8, e2m3: Array<UInt8, 24> }

prose.TrustedMarkup: MXFP6 with E2M3 elements, which have no infinity or NaN and reach 7.5.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn toMxFp6E2M3(xs: read Array<Float32, 32>) -> MxFp6E2M3Block

prose.TrustedMarkup: The MXFP6 E2M3 block of xs.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type MxFp6E3M2Block = { e8m0: UInt8, e3m2: Array<UInt8, 24> }

prose.TrustedMarkup: MXFP6 with E3M2 elements, which have no infinity or NaN and reach 28.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn toMxFp6E3M2(xs: read Array<Float32, 32>) -> MxFp6E3M2Block

prose.TrustedMarkup: The MXFP6 E3M2 block of xs.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type MxFp4Block = { e8m0: UInt8, e2m1: Array<UInt8, 16> }

prose.TrustedMarkup: MXFP4: E2M1 elements, which have no infinity or NaN and reach 6, two to a byte with element 2i in the low nibble of byte i.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn toMxFp4(xs: read Array<Float32, 32>) -> MxFp4Block

prose.TrustedMarkup: The MXFP4 block of xs.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type MxInt8Block = { e8m0: UInt8, int8: Array<Int8, 32> }

prose.TrustedMarkup: MXINT8: two's complement elements with an implicit scale of 2^-6. A narrowing keeps them within -127 to 127.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn toMxInt8(xs: read Array<Float32, 32>) -> MxInt8Block

prose.TrustedMarkup: The MXINT8 block of xs.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type NvFp4Block = { ue4m3: UInt8, e2m1: Array<UInt8, 8> }

prose.TrustedMarkup: NVFP4: 16 E2M1 elements, packed as in MxFp4Block, and a UE4M3 scale, an E4M3 code without a sign. A scale code of 127 is NaN; bit 7 is ignored.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn toNvFp4(xs: read Array<Float32, 16>) -> NvFp4Block

prose.TrustedMarkup: The NVFP4 block of xs. The scale is the largest magnitude divided by 6, rounded to UE4M3 and saturated; each element is its value divided by the scale, rounded to E2M1 and saturated. An infinity counts as the largest finite Float32, and a NaN sets the scale to 127 and every element to 0.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn packInt4(xs: read Array<Int8>) -> Array<UInt8>

prose.TrustedMarkup: xs as Int4 values, two to a byte with element 2i in the low nibble of byte i. Each value wraps to its low 4 bits, and an odd length leaves the last high nibble 0.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn int4At(packed: read Array<UInt8>, i: Int64) -> Int8

prose.TrustedMarkup: Element i of Int4 values that packInt4 packed, from -8 to 7.
